- [x] **TU.25.A — 🚨 ROOT: teach-phase GPU dispatch traffic EXCEEDS the donor link's drain rate — the buffer growth is STRUCTURAL, not a resync bug.** Receipts: net out **7,447 KB/s sustained** while the ENTIRE matrix set is only ~20MB — the flood is the fire-and-forget batched-Hebbian + compute-batch teach traffic itself (phase=_teachWordIntegrated/_teachHebbian on ela/kindergarten), not uploads. Gee's donor out=4,883MB in 12m51s (~6.3MB/s) with rtt 12,243ms; buffer sawtooths 142→419→606→659→686→713→740→758→785→820→838→865→892MB; CRITICAL DROPS climb 331→1095 in ~50s. The 30s backpressure AWAIT per frame doesn't shed load — it just stalls the dispatch pipeline while the queue keeps growing behind it. FIX CANDIDATES: (1) **fire-and-forget Hebbian frames should SHORT-CIRCUIT DROP (not await 30s) when bufferedAmount is over a soft threshold** — CPU CSR is authoritative, the GPU shadow self-heals via the (now-working) auto-resync on drain, so shedding shadow-Hebbian frames under pressure is safe by design; (2) **send-window cap** — bound total in-flight bytes per donor (e.g. 64MB) and pause the batched-Hebbian flush while over it (backpressure-aware flush already half-exists in the batch queue); (3) pace to the WSQ.4 measured linkDownMbps when present.

- [x] **TU.25.B — 🚨 heartbeat false-reaps the PRIMARY because the PING ITSELF is queued behind the saturated send buffer.** Kill cadence: 7 donor terminations in ~12.5min (one every ~107s — 10:04:51, 10:06:51, 10:08:21, 10:09:51, 10:12:52, 10:14:52, 10:16:22), ALWAYS the just-promoted primary mid-flood. At 400-900MB buffered and single-digit-MB/s drain, our outbound ping physically cannot REACH the donor for 60-120s → 2 missed pings guaranteed → terminate → reconnect → full re-init + re-upload → deeper flood → next kill. HBGRACE.2 forgives server-loop-block misses but NOT buffer-saturation misses (the +3-forgiven line proves grace works for the wrong cause). FIX: **don't count heartbeat misses against a donor while ws.bufferedAmount > threshold** (the ping never left the box — that's OUR congestion, not their death); bounded like HBGRACE (hard ceiling still kills a real corpse).

- [x] **TU.25.C — HBGRACE.3 mid-sync grace does NOT cover the PRIMARY's canonical initGpu upload path.** `_replicaSyncInFlight` marks only `_syncReplicaToDonor` targets; the primary receiving the 17-matrix canonical upload (initGpu → gpuSparseUpload) has no mid-sync marker, so the heartbeat killed it mid-upload every cycle (`terminating so failover can fire` + `sparse chunk send to a CLOSED donor socket (terminated mid-sync)`). FIX: mark the primary mid-sync during the canonical upload window (same bounded grace).

- [x] **TU.25.D — DF.7 promote-stronger CHURN AMPLIFIER: every reconnect of the same dying donor gets promoted PRIMARY mid-flood, orphaning the in-flight uploads to the old target.** Log: 7 consecutive `newcomer GPU is STRONGER (score 10.24 > current primary 0.73)` promotions — the battered survivor's score decays to 0.73 so ANY fresh socket wins; each promotion re-arms the FULL cortex upload; the old target's queued reqIds rot to the 180s timeout (all 17 timed out at 10:07:32-51; letter_to_phon burned 3×180s retries = ~9min). FIX CANDIDATES: (1) promotion HYSTERESIS — don't promote a newcomer while the current primary's canonical upload is in flight (or within N seconds of the last promotion); (2) on promotion/failover, CANCEL pending sparse reqIds targeted at the departed socket immediately instead of letting them hold 180s timers; (3) don't score a socket "stronger" purely because it's fresh (score should need ≥1 completed compute round-trip).

The confirmed-root-cause + shipped-fix narrative below is the resolution record.

- [ ] **TU.19 — donor/backpressure error storm + word_motor overflow (Gee-flagged from live dashboard 2026-07-06 ~10:22).** THREE distinct issues, all live on the box RIGHT NOW, all code-fix candidates (NOT benign teach-pin — I mis-triaged them for ~150 passes):
  - **[🚨 ISSUE-A — word_motor_sci CAPACITY OVERFLOW (NEW emission bug, science era)]:** live log `[emit] word_motor_sci capacity overflow — 3272 words exceed frozen band (cellSize=1). Words past index 582 cannot emit; raise word_motor fraction or lower DREAM_WORD_MOTOR_VOCAB_CAP.` The SPEAK.1 frozen bucket geometry for subject=sci froze at `bandSize=582 cellsPerWord=1 maxWords=582` — but science K vocab is 3272 words. **2690 science words physically cannot emit** (index >582 has no motor cells). This is why her science-era emissions lean on the older ELA/persona vocab — the science words literally have no output band. ROOT: `wordBucketCellSizeFor` froze the sci band from `bandSize/DREAM_WORD_MOTOR_VOCAB_CAP` but the sci band (582 cells) ÷ cap gives cellSize=1 with only 582 slots, far below the sci vocab count. FIX candidate: size the frozen band to the SUBJECT's actual vocab count (or raise the word_motor region fraction for multi-thousand-word subjects), not a global cap that starves per-subject bands.
  - **[🚨 ISSUE-B — BACKPRESSURE DROP STORM RETURNED + WORSE, and F5 auto-resync is FEEDING it]:** WS drops 14,715 (11.93/s), ws.bufferedAmount climbing 500MB→1159MB in a continuous sawtooth, GPU buffered 615/500MB, GPU shadow DIRTY, event-loop-lag max **51,002ms**. The TU.17 **F5 auto-resync is making it WORSE, not better**: on each drop it re-uploads `cortex_intraSynapses` (14.2MB) to "resync" — but it fires INTO an already-saturated buffer, stacking multiple 14.2MB uploads (reqId 205105+205106+206217+207319+208178… all intraSynapses, overlapping), which deepens the backpressure → more drops → arms another resync → repeat. Net out total = **301 GB** (10.5 MB/s sustained) = the same 14.2MB matrices re-uploaded thousands of times. The shadow NEVER clears DIRTY because the resync upload itself gets dropped. FIX candidate: (1) F5 must NOT arm a resync while `ws.bufferedAmount` is already over threshold — gate it on a DRAINED buffer; (2) coalesce/dedup in-flight intraSynapses uploads (never >1 pending); (3) the real root — DF.7 re-syncs a FULL 17-matrix+14.2MB replica on EVERY cell-pass, and science K has many rapid short cells (_teachDietClassification, _teachBodyPartFunction, _teachNaturalVsHumanMade… each a checkpoint+resync), so rapid cell-passes = re-upload storm. Throttle DF.7 replica re-sync to a min interval / only on meaningful drift, not every cell-pass.
  - **[⚠ ISSUE-C — consolidation DEADLINE-ABORT + donor choke]:** `[Consolidation] pass 95 … duration=31575ms · ⚠ DEADLINE-ABORT (DREAM_CONSOLIDATION_MAX_MS=30000ms)` — consolidation overran its 30s deadline (secondary to the loop being pinned by the upload storm). Donor `Gee` rtt **12,485ms**, buf **629 MB** queued, bind 16.0GB; `TheREV` rtt 108ms buf 0 but only 0.5 Gn/s (barely working) — the primary donor is choking on the 629MB backlog the storm created. Both are symptoms of A/B, not independent.
  - **[🔬 ISSUE-D — BUILD A GPU↔CPU PARITY HARNESS (Gee directive 2026-07-06):** *"wtf do you need to make a secondary script program to be able to comparie what the GPU/doner is doing versaes doing incorrectly versus messing up where our math is failing"* — CORRECT and it's the instrument we're missing. "GPU shadow DIRTY" is a single flag that conflates THREE independent failure modes we currently can't tell apart: **(1) STALE weights** — donor's uploaded matrices ≠ CPU master because uploads got backpressure-dropped (an I/O problem, ISSUE-B); **(2) WRONG GPU compute** — donor's shader produces a different result than the CPU for the SAME weights+inputs (a shader/precision bug); **(3) WRONG equational math** — the CPU master itself computes garbage (a model bug, e.g. bad CDF 9/7 / Hebbian / cross-projection). PLAN — `scripts/gpu-cpu-parity.mjs` (+ a small server diagnostic hook): (a) connect as a read-only observer; snapshot the CPU master's authoritative sparse matrix (e.g. cortex_intraSynapses) + hash it; (b) read back the donor's resident copy of the SAME matrix + hash → **hash match/mismatch isolates STALE (mode 1) instantly**; (c) if weights match, feed an identical deterministic input vector to BOTH the CPU propagate and the donor GPU propagate, diff the output (maxAbsErr / cosine / first-N divergent indices) → **nonzero diff on matched weights isolates WRONG-GPU-COMPUTE (mode 2)**; (d) run the CPU propagate against a hand-computed tiny reference (known 3×3 sparse case with known answer) → **CPU mismatch isolates WRONG-MATH (mode 3)**. Output: a one-line verdict `STALE | GPU-DIVERGENT | MATH-ERROR | CLEAN` + the numbers. This turns "DIRTY" from a dead flag into a pointed diagnosis, and tells us whether ISSUE-B's re-upload storm is even fixing anything (if it's mode 2/3, re-uploading is pointless). Building this next.
  - **PROCESS NOTE (mine):** I logged 150+ emission passes as "quiet" while these CRITICAL/backpressure lines scrolled — I treated the EventLoop-BLOCK + backpressure lines as the documented benign teach-pin class and never re-read that the drop COUNT was climbing into 5 figures or that a NEW word_motor overflow had appeared. Correction: infra-log scan is now part of every pass, not just grades+chat.

- Gee verbatim: *"the doner keeps dropping connection:"* + full 8:25-8:27PM log paste (deployed box, build d92f561, social/kindergarten cell, 1 donor Gee's remote RTX over the proxied WS).
- MECHANISM (read from the log): (1) TRIGGER — `[EventLoop] BLOCKED 13869ms` then `12555ms` on `phase=_teachPredictiveError cell=social/kindergarten`: a rare-but-huge synchronous pin (loop-delay p99=67ms healthy, but max=29,209ms) starves the proxied WS for 12-14s → server can't pong → "GPU compute client disconnected UNEXPECTEDLY" (proxied WS closed). (2) AMPLIFIER — every reconnect sets `_gpuShadowDirty` → FULL 85.2MB `cortex_intraSynapses` re-upload (14 chunks) + "Main tick paused while the canonical sparse upload runs"; a second 12.5s pin lands mid-upload → `read ECONNRESET ×32` → drops again → re-upload again = churn. Each drop = full 85MB re-upload (NO per-matrix dirty tracking — the queued deep cure deliberately never blind-shipped).
- CONTEXT: the 2026-07-13 pin fixes (propagateChunked adaptive-slice, _teachLateralInhibition 61MB-per-pair GC pooling, _memoryHeartbeat episodic-scan LIMIT) are in the deployed build, yet 12-14s pins persist on `_teachPredictiveError` — so the residual pinner is EITHER a still-unsliced op inside the predictive-error phase (crumb task line ~3481 flagged "_teachPredictiveError ... sync hebbianUpdate UNSLICED 61M-row intra ops — prime suspects") OR the 85MB resync serialization/GC itself running under the phase label.
- CONSTRAINTS: no fresh walk currently (Gee 2026-07-14); per-matrix dirty re-upload is "too risky to blind-ship before a clean fresh walk" (DS.5 remaining). So the SAFE lever is killing the PIN (slice/defer whatever synchronous op in _teachPredictiveError pins 12-14s at 61M), which stops the drop at its trigger and breaks the churn without touching GPU-shadow correctness.
- TODO: (a) code-read _teachPredictiveError — find the unsliced synchronous op (sync hebbianUpdate on the 61M intra? predictive-error fill over full cluster.size?) and time-slice it like the adaptive Hebbian/propagate paths; (b) confirm whether the resync 85MB re-upload runs synchronously enough to pin (it's chunked+paced, so likely not the 12s pinner, but verify); (c) report findings before shipping. Deploys on Update & Savestart (keep weights) — no fresh walk, no donor rebuild.
- **DIAGNOSIS (code-read 2026-07-14, corrects the initial guess):** `_teachPredictiveError` is ALREADY time-sliced (propagateChunked chunkRows=65536 + `_hebbianUpdateChunked`, both yield) — NOT the direct pinner. The intra matrix is `new SparseMatrix(size, size)` (cluster.js:594) = genuinely 61M×61M at the deployed cortex (the "349k rows" comment in the method is STALE pre-full-size). So predictive-error holds ~1.46GB of pooled Float64Array scratches (3 × 488MB at 61M) + 565MB external. The 12-29s BLOCKED (loop p99=67ms healthy, max=29,209ms — rare+huge = classic major-GC signature) is a V8 STOP-THE-WORLD major GC under that multi-GB heap pressure on the CPU-only coordinator box (Xeon, 32GB, no GPU), starving the proxied WS → donor can't pong → drop. Amplifier confirmed: each reconnect fires a full 85MB cortex_intraSynapses re-upload (no per-matrix dirty tracking) → churn. This is the documented "61M-vs-349k / CPU-coordinator event cost" residual. NO cheap slice-fix (can't slice a GC pause). LEVERS (each a different risk/reward — Gee decision): (1) proxy/donor timeout tolerance so the donor rides through a 15-30s pin without dropping (config, Red — kills the DROP + churn at the symptom, zero training change); (2) churn-debounce so rapid drop→reconnect cycles coalesce instead of each firing 85MB (safe band-aid); (3) reduce GC pressure at 61M (move predictive-error/teach bookkeeping scratches off-heap or to a worker — bigger change); (4) per-matrix dirty re-upload (the deep cure, but "too risky to blind-ship before a clean fresh walk"). A churn-dropping donor no longer fires a full 85MB `cortex_intraSynapses` re-upload PER reconnect — repeats collapse to one throttled re-upload. ## [~] word_motor BAND OVERFLOW — learned words silenced (Gee 2026-07-14)
- Gee verbatim: *"this needs fixed: sounds like erroniuos bumbing down of her capabilities:art-vocab-exceeds-band issue"*
- LOG: `[emit] word_motor_art capacity overflow — band holds 2270 words (2270 cells / 1 per word) but subject has 2548; 277 words past index 2271 CANNOT emit.` She LEARNED 2548 art words but the per-subject emission band only carves 2270 cells → 277 known words have no motor bucket → cannot be emitted. Erroneous capability cap (violates never-dumb-her-down).
- The log's stock "remedy: grow the language cortex / add GPUs" is a PUNT — word_motor is ~6% of the 61M cortex (~3.68M cells), vastly more than any subject's vocab, so a 2270-cell art band means the per-subject CARVE is undersizing, NOT a real capacity ceiling. Fix the carve (vocab-aware band sizing) so every learned word gets a bucket — never silence a word she knows.
- TODO: find the word_motor sub-band carve (TU.20.1 proportional) + `wordBucketCellSizeFor`/`wordMotorBandName`/`_ensureWordBucketMap` + the `bStart >= bandEnd break` overflow; make band sizing cover each subject's ACTUAL vocab (the 3.68M region has room); verify by reading, no walk.
- SCOPE (Gee 2026-07-14): *"that needs fioxed ciriculum wide"* — fix ALL subjects' bands, not just art. Art overflowed first (heaviest vocab) but math/science/social/ela/life/every subject will overflow as vocab grows across grades. Band sizing must cover each subject's actual (growing) vocab curriculum-wide, K→PhD.

### ROOT CAUSE (code-read 2026-07-14) + APPROACH A DECIDED (Gee):
- EMISSION runs on the DENSE ~349K language cortex (`cortexCluster`), NOT the 61M sparse main cortex. `word_motor` = top 6% of that cluster (cluster.js:730-731 `wmStart=floor(s*0.940)`, `wmEnd=s`) => ~20,954 cells total at s≈349K.
- Per-subject sub-bands carved by a HARDCODED weight table `WM_DEMAND=[['ela',1.25],['math',0.75],['sci',1.5],['soc',1.2],['art',0.65],['life',0.65]]` (cluster.js:742-755), sum=6.0. Art's slice = 6% × (0.65/6) × 349K ≈ 2270 cells.
- `wordBucketCellSizeFor` (emit.js:917-942) pins cellsPerWord = `max(1, floor(bandSize/50000))` = 1 when bandSize<50K → art holds 2270 words at the MINIMUM packing. Art vocab=2548 → 277 silenced. cellsPerWord can't go below 1 → HARD WALL, not a ratio bug.
- CURRICULUM-WIDE: every subject's vocab is append-only + grows K→PhD (`_ensureWordBucketMap` curriculum.js:11242-11284); full-curriculum emission vocab is tens of thousands of words >> 21K cells. Every band overflows eventually. The 349K language cortex is simply too small to bucket the full vocab.

## 2026-08-14 — HONEST PROGRESS TELEMETRY (the 85% was a stopwatch, and the frozen spikes were by design)

Gee (verbatim): *"she is at 85% again and its not ticking up anymore.. it was 12-15 secs for each percent upto *5% then it never gets to 86%"* → *"is she fine?"* → *"build #1 and #2 while she does. we can do an update and save start later"*

**WHY THIS EXISTS.** Twice Gee had to ask whether his brain was alive, and both times the answer required reading raw JSON and reasoning about it — once WRONGLY. The instruments were the problem, not the brain.

**WHAT THE 85% ACTUALLY WAS.** `dashboard.html:3434` renders `~N% [time-est] · 0 phases reported · (in progress, server phase counter stuck)` — elapsed-time ÷ expected-duration. It climbs ~1% per ~13s, saturates, and stops. It never measured her at all. `cellPhasesCompleted` only ticks when an OUTERMOST phase FINISHES, and a K cell's first phase runs tens of minutes, so the real counter sat at 0 and the dashboard fell back to a stopwatch.

**WHAT THE FROZEN SPIKES ACTUALLY WERE.** `brain-server.js:4270` — while `cortexCluster._probeGateActive`, the main tick returns EARLY and dispatches no `compute_batch` ("cortex owns GPU exclusively for the probe window"). `totalSpikes` freezing, `gpuHits` sticking, `batchTiming.samples` stopping are all CORRECT during a cell. **I diagnosed this as "her neurons stopped firing" on the previous walk — that was wrong.** The donor drown found alongside it was real and the D.1/D.2 fixes measurably worked (RTT 6,348→816ms, patternSheds 217,015→0, buffer 19.4MB→0, `unhealthy`→false, MB/s 3.87→2.14), but the frozen-spike alarm was a designed pause misread as a freeze.

**AND D.3 WAS BLIND WHERE IT MATTERED.** The watchdog was placed INSIDE `_gpuBatch` — which the tick never calls while paused — so it reported `batchStall: null` while spikes sat frozen. It could not fire in the one situation it was built for.

- **P.1 real progress signal.** `cellPhasesStarted` — outermost phases ENTERED in the current cell, self-resetting on cell-key change, so it moves the instant real work begins instead of after the first phase completes. `vocabProgress` — the live `{label, taught, total, pct, elapsedSec, lastWord}` position inside the running vocab list; the teach loop already computed taught/total for its log line and then discarded it. Held on ONE mutated object (no per-word allocation), updated every word (not every 5th like the event broadcast — the point is that it visibly moves during a long phase), nulled on list completion so a stale position is never reported.
- **P.2 pause-aware stall detection.** Moved out of `_gpuBatch` into `state.js _getProfilingState`, which always runs, and split into two fields that were previously indistinguishable from outside: **`batchPaused`** `{reason, sinceLastBatchMs, cell, expected:true}` for a DESIGNED pause (probe-gate / canonical upload — frozen spikes here are CORRECT), versus **`batchStall`** `{stalledMs, lastOkAt, donorBufferedMB, expected:false}` for a donor connected, nothing paused, and completions stopped anyway — the only state that means something is wrong. The in-`_gpuBatch` copy is now pause-gated too so a designed pause can never train anyone to ignore the alarm.

**VERIFY (no-tests LAW):** `node --check` PASS ×3; ESM `import()` on curriculum (26 exports, `getCurriculumStatus` live); both server mixins load (state 15, gpu 56); all 8 wiring points grepped present; bundle rebuilt KEYLESS (0 live-key hits) carrying `_vocabProgress`.

- **P.5 REAL PROGRESS BARS, NOT TIMERS.** Gee (verbatim): *"io think we also need to make the progress bars real progress bars not timers"*. P.1 published honest data; the dashboard still rendered a stopwatch. `dashboard.html` computed `Math.min(85, round(elapsedMin / EXPECTED_K_CELL_MIN * 85))` — **hard-capped at 85**, which is literally why the bar could never reach 86% and why it saturated and froze on a brain that was teaching normally. It measured wall-clock, never work. Rewired onto the real signals: composite of `cellPhasesStarted` (phases ENTERED) plus the in-flight `vocabProgress` fraction over the expected phase count, capped at 99 so it can never claim done before the cell passes; falls back to `vocabProgress.pct` alone when no phase has registered yet; and keeps the time estimate ONLY as a last resort, now labelled `[time-est — no real signal yet, this is a stopwatch]` so it can never be mistaken for progress again. Scope hazard closed: the sibling `EXPECTED_PHASES_PER_CELL` lives in a DIFFERENT `<script>` block and not at its top level, so it is read through a `typeof` guard with a local fallback instead of throwing ReferenceError. Verified by extracting and parsing every classic inline script block (both OK) and by a LAW grep for task-numbers/operator-name in the public HTML (0).

- **P.6 EXACT PHASE TOTALS, NEVER AN ESTIMATE.** Gee (verbatim): *"wtf is this expected cells per phase or what evr it was? should it be exact # per cell per grade? why are we estimating"*. FIX: `_cellRunner` now reads the DECLARED count straight from the resolved runner's own source (`Function.prototype.toString` + `_phaseTick(` count) — valid because cell runners are NOT auto-wrapped (the constructor wrap tracks only `_teach*` plus two named probes), so `raw` is the authored function; cached per cell key and logged once. Donor: `rttMs` **6,348**, `bufferedKB` **19,394** and climbing, `unhealthy: true`. Outbound **11,089 MB in 47 min = 3.87 MB/s**, `msgOut` 74,172 → **153.1 KB AVERAGE MESSAGE**. `patternSheds` +110/sec. Meanwhile the SERVER was healthy: `stepTimeMs` 663, eventLoop p50 21ms, ticks +210/min — the loop span freely with nothing behind it.

**ROOT.** The teach lane ships `write_spike_slice`/`write_current_slice` as JSON arrays of raw integers — 153 KB/message, 3.87 MB/s — into a socket the donor cannot drain. The CHAT.1 lesson (emission went zero-payload / sparse-index binary) was never applied to the TEACH lane. Compounding it: at `SUBSTEPS=24` the donor is busy ~360ms per batch and CANNOT READ ITS SOCKET WHILE COMPUTING, so ~1.4MB piles up per batch.

**OWNED HONESTLY.** Today's two changes moved the bottleneck rather than closing it: Rev's substeps 3→24 made the donor 8× slower to service its socket, and the tick-gap yield fix freed the server loop to push teach frames FASTER. The tick collapse (5,526→663ms) was real, but "running smoothly" was reported without checking `totalSpikes` — the stall was already underway at the time.

**DONOR BINARY — Gee's question answered by verification:** `git diff donor-v0.3.11..main -- donor-app/` is **EMPTY**; `html/compute.html` unchanged. **Nothing Rev or we shipped today requires a donor rebuild.** The connected donor (`engineBackend: cuda` = native v0.3.11) is correct for all of it.

**DEPLOY CONSTRAINT honored:** Gee deploys via dashboard buttons only and cannot set env vars on the box, so every fix ships as a **CODE DEFAULT** with the env var retained purely as an override.

- **D.1 pattern-lane flood control** (`gpu.js _donorPatternLaneOpen`): teach-throttle default **20ms → 100ms**, plus **ADAPTIVE back-off** — the interval scales by how far the donor's buffer is past its link cap and by smoothed RTT >1s, bounded ×16 so it can never become an effective mute. A fixed throttle could not know the link was drowning; it kept firing into a full socket while the shed counter absorbed the lie. These frames are per-iteration ephemeral and were already ~100% shed, so pacing them costs nothing real and returns the link to `compute_batch` + hebbian deltas + acks + pings.

- **D.3 silent-stall watchdog** (`gpu.js` + `state.js`): the failure was invisible BY SHAPE — every early return in `_gpuBatch` hands back `null` silently, so "never dispatched" and "healthy idle" are indistinguishable, and the 180s timeout can only fire for batches actually SENT. Now the last SUCCESSFUL completion is stamped (`_lastBatchOkMs`, set only on a real resolve — the timeout path uses the raw resolve so a timing-out donor can never look alive); if a donor is connected and completions stop for >30s it logs a CRITICAL naming buffer/RTT/substeps and surfaces `batchStall` in state. `batchTiming` (the earlier send→reply stopwatch) is now surfaced too — it existed but was never wired into the payload.

## 2026-08-14 — EVERY GRADE LEARNS DEFINITIONS LIKE K (via the dream-trickle, not a 2.2h blocking wall)

Gee (verbatim): *"and why the fuck does it take so long to do kvocab, but every other grade doesnt do a vocab?"* → *"i think option 1 is best,, but i dont want to make k like every other grade... should we instead make every other greade like k"* → *"build it, write the todo fully, and DO NOT FORGET TO BUILD THE TASDK LIST IN THE CLI SO I CAN FOLLOW ALONG ON WHERE U ARE!!! YOU FORGOT TO DO THIS LAST TIME"*

**THE FINDING.** Kindergarten was the ONLY grade running a BLOCKING upfront definition seed. `curriculum.js` fired `_teachWordDefinitions(K_VOCABULARY)` — all 2,247 words × every definition sense — BEFORE a single cell ran. Every other grade got prefetch-ONLY (a fire-and-forget dictionary CACHE warm that binds nothing) with definition binding left lazy. The K block's own comments admitted the upfront Hebbian had been **DROPPED** once for basin-blur risk ("~70k cross-bindings would dense-web the sem region"), called it "BONUS that may be net-negative", and it was later partially re-added at reps 6→2 as "just the seed" — the blocking-at-boot cost was never revisited.

**MEASURED LIVE** (deployed box, build `6fbb992d`): `kVocabTaught` 117 → 143 over 90.3s = **~17 words/min** → K alone = **~2.2 hours** of pre-cell blocking on every fresh walk.

**WHY NOT THE LITERAL "make every grade like K":** the 19 grade vocab files total **49,921 words** (K 2,247 · G1 2,022 · G2 2,083 · G3 1,439 · G4 2,148 · G5 2,030 · G6 2,698 · G7 3,650 · G8 2,914 · G9 4,255 · G10 4,198 · G11 4,171 · G12 4,093 · C1 2,544 · C2 2,037 · C3 1,941 · C4 2,092 · grad 1,786 · phd 1,573). At 17 words/min that is **48.9 hours ≈ 2 DAYS** of blocking pre-cell seed. Gee's instinct (more depth, not less) was right; the PLACEMENT was the problem.

**BUILT — same content, better lane.** The mechanism already existed and was BETTER than K's blocking seed: the dream-trickle binds `_teachWordDefinition(word, {reps: 4, ...})` — **deeper than the blocking seed's reps:1** — with a retry queue for API timeouts and a `_dwOverBudget` window-budget gate. Its only flaw: the queue source was hardcoded to `K_VOCABULARY`, so 18 grades never touched it.

- **V.1 queue generalized** — the K-only lazy init is now a FALLBACK for a boot race / resumed mid-K state; the queue is fed by grade-start enqueues. Field name `_kVocabQueue` deliberately KEPT (it is persisted in saved weights — renaming would orphan every in-flight queue on load).
- **V.2 per-grade enqueue** — each grade enqueues ITS OWN vocabulary at ITS OWN grade start, beside the existing prefetch. Grade-appropriateness is now STRUCTURAL, not filtered: advanced vocabulary cannot be in the queue before its grade begins, so the corpus-bleed rule holds by construction.
- **V.3 K de-blocked** — the blocking upfront pass is skipped; K's 2,247 words route through the same trickle at reps:4. `DREAM_K_UPFRONT_SEED=1` restores the old blocking pass.
- **V.4 drain rate** — `DREAM_TRICKLE_BATCH` 25 → 120, env-tunable. 25 was sized when the queue only ever held K's words. The per-word `_dwOverBudget` check INSIDE the loop is what actually bounds cost (it stops mid-batch when the window's time is spent), so a bigger batch raises the ceiling without lengthening a dream window. **NOT claimed as tuned** — real drain rate must be watched live.
- **V.5 dedup + carry-forward** — `_enqueueDefinitionSeed()` dedups on BOTH axes (already-bound via the persisted `_definitionTaughtWords`, and already-queued) because AoA-ordered grade bands overlap heavily; appends rather than replaces so a prior grade's undrained tail survives; idempotent per grade.

**NET:** ~49.9K words of multi-def Hebbian across the walk instead of 2,247 (**22×**), at reps:4 instead of reps:1-2 (**deeper**), with the ~2.2h pre-cell wall **removed**.

**VERIFY (no-tests LAW):** `node --check` PASS; real ESM `import()` (26 exports) with `_enqueueDefinitionSeed` / `_dreamWindow` / `_teachWordDefinition` / `_teachWordDefinitions` all confirmed on the prototype; all three wiring points grepped present; bundle rebuilt KEYLESS (0 live-key hits) carrying the helper + banner.

**OPEN (V.8, needs Gee's SAVESTART):** confirm the walk reaches its first cell in seconds rather than ~2.2h, and that `💤 dream trickle: N words processed … N words remaining in the definition-seed queue (grades enqueued: …)` lines show the queue actually draining across grades. If it lags, raise `DREAM_TRICKLE_BATCH`.

## 2026-08-14 — TOLERABLE / REV PR #3 MERGED (substeps 3 → 24 at biological scale — the GPU idles 98.5% of every tick)

Gee (verbatim): *"Rev made another PR, same thing update local and both repos"*

github PR #3 — *"The GPU is idle 98.5% of every tick — measured on the live brain"* — head `8cab418`, 1 commit, 1 file, **+36/−1**, conflict-free. Fetched via `refs/pull/3/head` → local `pr3/head`, merged `--no-ff` into `feature/merge-rev-pr3-substeps-0814` off main, cascaded develop → main, pushed to BOTH remotes. Authorship preserved (`Reverend Dr Tolerant`).

**THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE LINE:** `_SUBSTEPS_AUTO` at the `>1,000,000` neuron tier, **3 → 24**. Sub-1M tiers deliberately UNCHANGED (never measured against them).

**HIS MEASUREMENT (live deployed brain, 306M neurons, one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER):** `stepTimeMs 3010.5` (one tick takes three seconds) · `ticks/sec 0.728` · `cpuPercent 6` (CPU idle) · `eventLoopLagMs 4` (loop NOT starved) · `gpuMisses 0` (donor answers every batch) · donor self-reported `20.3 Gneurons/sec`. Arithmetic: 7 clusters × 3 substeps × 306M = 919M neuron-steps/tick, which at 20.3 Gn/s is **45ms of real GPU math inside a 3010ms tick — the GPU works 1.5% of the time**. The other ~2965ms is round-trip (dispatch, per-cluster readback, ack handling, state broadcast) and is **FIXED PER TICK regardless of substeps**.

**WHY THE OLD LADDER WAS BACKWARDS:** it LOWERED substeps as the brain grew (10 → 5 → 3) on the assumption that more neurons mean more per-substep cost to throttle. But the throttle only ever shrank the payload, never the overhead — so at biological scale it maximised the fraction of wall-clock spent on protocol. The bigger the brain, the MORE substeps should ride per round-trip, because the round-trip is the expensive part. 24 substeps ≈ 360ms of GPU math per ~3300ms tick: **8× the brain steps for ~10% more wall clock**. Deliberately not pushed to the ~60 the arithmetic allows, because `compute_batch` has a real timeout and a donor stalling mid-batch trips the zombie-kick path.

**THIS IS THE FIRST OF REV'S PRs THAT CHANGES DEPLOYED BEHAVIOUR BY DEFAULT** (PR #1 landed on the browser-only brain; PR #2's attention relay is opt-in). Watch after deploy: `compute_batch` timeouts, donor disconnects mid-batch, dashboard responsiveness. **ROLLBACK IS ONE ENV VAR — `DREAM_SUBSTEPS=3`** (the knob PR #2 added, which is what makes this safe to try).

**NO FRESH WALK, NO BUNDLE.** No weight-format or geometry change → Update & SAVESTART. `server/brain-server.js` is server-side CommonJS and not in the esbuild entry graph, so no browser bundle rebuild. `brain-server.js` IS in `BRAIN_CODE_FILES` so the code hash moves; `DREAM_KEEP_STATE=1` (Savestart) bypasses the hash check and weights survive. VERIFY: `node --check server/brain-server.js` PASS; diff confirmed to be the single `_SUBSTEPS_AUTO` constant plus its rationale comment.
